title: He wasn’t trained.
paragraphs:
He wasn’t trained.
He wasn’t famous.
He wasn’t ready.
And here’s the part that should disturb you—
He didn’t even have a real weapon.

You feel disqualified.
Unnoticed.
Too broken.
Too late.

You look at your life and think,
“God can’t use this version of me.”
But Shamgar didn’t wait to become impressive.
And that’s where the tension begins.
Because deep inside, you know God is calling you too…
Something you don’t want anyone to see.
It’s not just lack of skill.

“You’ve already messed up too much.”
“You’re not clean enough.”
“You’re not consistent enough.”
“You’re not worthy.”
Because you think God only uses polished people.
But that’s not what Scripture shows.
“After him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad, and he also saved Israel.” — Judges 3:31
Just God working through a man who had something in his hand.
Some scholars interpret Shamgar’s background as possibly influenced by foreign culture—his name “son of Anath” may even hint at connections outside pure Israelite identity.
God didn’t wait for Shamgar to become impressive.
God moved through him as he was willing.
But here’s where it gets uncomfortable…

Hidden sin.
Private compromise.
Double life patterns.
Secret habits you keep feeding.
And you’re losing strength not because God is absent—
…but because sin is quietly draining you.
“Your iniquities have separated you from your God; your sins have hidden his face from you…” — Isaiah 59:2
Not because God stops loving you—
…but because sin distorts your intimacy with Him.
“This is just who I am now.”
Because Shamgar points to something greater.
Shamgar used a piece of wood to defeat enemies.
Jesus used wood to defeat sin.
“God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.” — 2 Corinthians 5:21
And He carried them to the cross.
You don’t clean yourself first, then come to God.
Because no oxgoad can fix your heart.
No discipline alone can erase your guilt.
No hiding can heal your soul.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
What is God already asking me to surrender?
Because the same God who used Shamgar…
is not limited by your past.
But He is waiting for your surrender.
You don’t need a better version of yourself.
And watch what God can do with what’s in your hand—
and what’s finally released from your heart.
